problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,-1)$ and passes through the point $(2,1).$
worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(1,-1),$ we substitute $h=1$ and $k=-1$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =4p(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(2,1),$ so we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=1$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (1+1)^{2} & =4p(2-1) \\ 4 & =4p \\ p & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (y+1)^{2} & =4(1)(x-1) \\ (y+1)^{2} & =4(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$
